Types of PID Equations Compared Side by Side

Types of PID controllers differ in how the same three actions are written: Parallel (independent), Ideal (ISA or non interacting) and Series (interacting). The table puts the three equations together so you can see exactly where Kp, τi and τd act, with e as the error and m as the controller output.

TypeController output equationEffect of KpInteraction
Parallelm = Kp e + (1/τi) ∫e dt + τd de/dtProportional term onlyNone, all terms independent
Ideal (ISA)m = Kp [ e + (1/τi) ∫e dt + τd de/dt ]All three termsτi and τd act only on their own terms
Seriesm = Kp [ (1 + τd/τi) e + (1/τi) ∫e dt + τd de/dt ]All three termsτi and τd also change the proportional term

Converting Series Settings to Ideal Form

When a legacy series controller is replaced by an ideal form controller, convert the tuning values with these standard relations:

  1. Kp ideal = Kp series × (1 + τd/τi)
  2. τi ideal = τi series + τd series
  3. τd ideal = (τi series × τd series) ÷ (τi series + τd series)

If τd is zero, all three forms give the same result, so a PI loop moves between controller brands without retuning. The other common way to list the types of PID control is by modes used: P, PI, PD and full PID.
